approachQuestion.prompt:
New device sightings. A forward-only stream contains n signed 64-bit device IDs. Return the number of distinct IDs seen. IDs have no smaller bounded universe. There are 1 <= n <= 200,000 observations; order is arbitrary and duplicates are allowed. Do not retain or rewind the stream. Minimize expected total time under the following explicit model, then asymptotic peak auxiliary storage. A resizable hash set provides expected amortized constant-time membership/insertion, with linear peak storage in its distinct stored keys, including resizing; hashing a fixed-size ID costs constant time. The expectation is over the hash implementation, not a distribution of device IDs. Only the returned count is output.

Example 1: Input: [40,-2,40,7,-2]. Output: 3.
Example 2: Input: [9,9,9]. Output: 1.

options.text: Maintain a hash set of previously observed IDs, insert each observation, and return the set size.
options.feedback: Set membership retains exactly the distinction needed for future sightings. The stated hash model gives efficient aggregate processing without assumptions about the input order.

options.text: Keep a list of distinct IDs; compare each observation with the list and append only if absent.
options.feedback: It is correct, but an all-distinct stream repeatedly scans an increasingly long list. The supplied set model avoids those repeated full comparisons.

options.text: Count the first observation and then count each ID different from the immediately preceding ID.
options.feedback: For [4,7,4], this counts 3, but only two distinct devices occur. Duplicates need not be consecutive.

options.text: Use a hash set, but remove an ID whenever a repeated sighting is found; return the final size.
options.feedback: For [9,9], this removes the only key and returns 0 instead of 1. Seeing an ID again does not make it unseen.

feedback.reason: A cost guarantee must name its model; hash-based expected efficiency is different from an unconditional worst-case guarantee.
details: Start with an empty hash set. Insert each observed ID if absent and retain every distinct key through the end. Return the set size. Use the expected amortized operations and peak resize storage given in the problem.

Repeated sightings do not create additional stored keys. A stream of n distinct IDs reaches the largest set, whereas one ID repeated n times still needs n membership operations but only one stored key. Expected hashing affects runtime guarantees, not the requirement to count distinct identities exactly.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For hash-distinct-ids, let d be the final number of distinct IDs. Under the stated hash model, choose expected total time and peak auxiliary space for n observations. Include set growth, current event and counters. Input and returned count are excluded. No sorting or recursion is performed.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard bound for the complete execution. Count peak simultaneously live auxiliary storage; exclude supplied input and required output.
Word arithmetic, indexing, and copying one fixed-size element take constant time. No hashing or recursion is used.

options.text: Expected O(n) total time, O(d) auxiliary space
Worst-case O(1) total time, O(d) auxiliary space
Expected O(n²) total time, O(d) auxiliary space
Expected O(n) total time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Perform n expected-amortized set operations and retain d distinct keys.
details: There are n expected amortized constant-cost set operations, so expected total time is O(n), including resizing. The set stores d distinct fixed-size keys, and the model also bounds peak resize storage by O(d). Since n>=1, d>=1. This is not a deterministic guarantee against every collision pattern; no input-distribution assumption was made.
“Worst-case O(1) total time, O(d) auxiliary space”: All n observations must be consumed, and the hash guarantee is expected amortized rather than constant time for the entire run.
“Expected O(n²) total time, O(d) auxiliary space”: This is a loose upper bound under the supplied expected model, not its tight total guarantee.
“Expected O(n) total time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The set retains all d distinct keys; outputting only a count does not remove that state.
